proposal: The Mandate recommends reversing the 2010 federalization of student lending and working with Congress to spin off Federal Student Aid and its loan obligations to a new government corporation, with federal loans assigned to the Treasury Department for collections and defaults. It also urges considering a return to private lending backed by government guarantees.
remaining: Legislation creating a professionally governed government corporation to hold FSA and the loan portfolio, with a Senate-confirmed head and board: none found.
Treasury phases beyond defaulted-loan collections (non-defaulted loans, other FSA functions) remain undated.

Return to private lending with government guarantees (the Mandate's preferred option) or the fallback consolidation into one loan program: no action toward private lending found; see c11-08 for the consolidation and borrowing-limit pieces.

status_summary: As of 2026-10-07 Federal Student Aid remains inside ED and no government corporation exists. On 2026-03-19 ED and Treasury announced a Federal Student Assistance Partnership, an interagency agreement. In its first phase Treasury takes operational responsibility for collecting defaulted federal student loans; later phases may extend Treasury support to loans not in default and other FSA functions, with no dates given. Federal News Network reports the later stages could include FAFSA administration and puts the portfolio at about $1.7 trillion. A House committee package advanced in July 2026 includes a bill to codify moving student loan administration to Treasury. No action toward private, government-guaranteed lending was found in the sources reviewed.

timeline.event: Some Federal Student Aid staff begin working at Treasury (month only given in source).

ED and Treasury announce the Federal Student Assistance Partnership. Phase 1: Treasury takes operational responsibility for collecting defaulted federal student loans and supports returning borrowers to repayment. Later phases are undated and conditioned on practicability and law. The release cites no statute.
House Education and Workforce Committee Republicans release a ten-bill package that includes a bill moving federal student loan administration to Treasury (bill numbering differs between sources).
